newsitem.title: USA: Most U.S. debt futures end lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Most U.S. debt futures end lower on profit-taking.

text.p: Most U.S. debt futures closed lower on profit-taking after five days of straight gains made traders slightly nervous ahead of the weekend, analysts said.
"They don't want to get too positioned at the upper end of the range," one T-bond futures trader said. "We get toppy everytime we get close to 6.75 percent (cash bond yield)."
Traders said technical weakness was compounded by nervousness ahead of next week's schedule of U.S. economic reports, with several citing next Friday's employment data.
"We have some concerns about the numbers going forward," another trader said.
The market's concerns about next week's numbers overshadowed end-of-quarter buying, they said.
Traders attributed quarter-end buying and follow-through Asian and European buying with December T-bonds' early-morning rally to 110-10/32.

Some traders noted that the strength in the U.S. dollar helped attract investors in the U.S. T-bond market. However, the buying failed to generate much enthusiasm or volume at the upper end of the range.
"That's been typical all week," one analyst said. "It's been a grind up."
"The new buying ran out of steam," a trader said. "People are a little less inclined to get involved in the market due to the volume and open interest."
Before pit trade opened, several analysts were expressing caution on eurodollars' upside potential.
December Eurodollars eased to 94.22 in a move that was largely powered by the decline in the T-bond futures market. December T-bonds fell to 109-12/32 late in the day, near support at 109-10/32.
Traders said profit-taking occurred after the contract dipped below Thursday's high of 109-31/32.

At the end of pit trade, December T-bonds were off 11/32 at 109-15/32, T-notes eased 6/32 to 107-15/32, muni-bonds dropped 13/32 to 114-04/32, December T-bills lost two bps to 94.79, and Eurodollars eased one bp to 94.23. --Derivatives Desk 312-408-8750 E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
